title: LeBron James' 500th Playoff Steal Sparks Wild Fan Reactions on Wednesday - NewsBreak
text:
By Reign Amurao ,
1 hours ago LeBron James of the Los Angeles Lakers continues to break records and make history. On Wednesday, against the Houston Rockets for Game 5 of the first round of the NBA playoffs, James became the first player in league history to record 500 career playoff steals. His longevity and dominance have helped him set new records in the regular season and playoffs.
In order to advance to the next round, where they may face the Oklahoma City Thunder, James and the Lakers hope to overcome the Rockets. They have the upper hand with a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series. LA has leaned on the four-time champion to take over, since Luka Doncic remains sidelined with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
After LeBron James reached a new milestone, NBA fans couldn’t help but react to what he did. Here are some of what the fans said.
“ Bron on a level of his own with 2 and 3 being teammates. Summarizes his career well,” a fan said .
“He really came for every record 😭😭🤞🏾🫶🏽” another fan commented .
“500 steals in the playoffs is just unfair Man’s been picking pockets since before half this league was born. King don’t ask he takes. Simple as that,” one fan commented .
“LeBron doing ‘all time leader’ things in literally every category 😂” someone commented .
“Incredible milestone for LeBron 500 playoff steals solidifies his all‑time defensive impact,” a comment read .
“Just constantly sets new records 🐐” one fan said .
LeBron James Weighed in on the Debate With Michael Jordan For the longest time, LeBron James and Michael Jordan have been part of the GOAT debate. It’s usually the two basketball icons that are part of the conversations. In an exclusive article written by ESPN’s Dave McMenamin, the topic of the GOAT debate came up again.
James shut down the talk and explained that they have different ways of playing the game. The Lakers star also clarified that he never compared himself to the former Chicago Bulls star.
“I never have compared myself to MJ because our games are totally different,” James said . “I have been a point-forward/forward-point my whole life. I have always looked for the pass. MJ kind of looked for the shot. Not kind of, he did. He looked for the shot.”
Despite clarifying things, fans and experts still argue about who is better between them.
